questions.q: What can Oracle GoldenGate do that Data Guard fundamentally cannot?
options: Replicate heterogeneously between different database platforms, such as Oracle to SQL Server or MySQL to Oracle
Provide a read-only copy of an Oracle database
Ship redo from a primary to a standby
Run entirely without any licensing requirement
questions.explain: Data Guard only works Oracle-to-Oracle at the whole-database level; GoldenGate's logical, log-based capture lets it replicate across different database platforms entirely.

questions.q: How does GoldenGate's Extract process capture changes from the source database?
options: By reading the source database's own transaction logs directly, rather than using triggers or polling tables
By taking a full nightly export of the entire database
By polling every table every second for differences
By intercepting network traffic between the application and the database
questions.explain: GoldenGate uses log-based change data capture, reading transaction logs (redo logs on Oracle, binary logs on MySQL, etc.) to find committed changes with low overhead.

questions.q: What is GoldenGate's Replicat process able to do that Data Guard's redo apply or SQL Apply cannot?
options: Transform data during apply — renaming columns, changing data types, or filtering rows
Apply changes without ever reading a trail file
Run without any capture process at all
Replicate data with zero possible latency under any configuration
questions.explain: Replicat can transform data as it applies it to the target, a capability Data Guard's block-level or SQL-level apply mechanisms don't offer.

questions.q: Is GoldenGate's Data Pump component the same thing as Oracle's expdp/impdp Data Pump export/import utility?
options: No — they share a name only; GoldenGate's Data Pump ships trail files across the network, unrelated to the export/import utility
Yes, they are exactly the same tool used in two different contexts
GoldenGate's Data Pump replaced expdp/impdp entirely in modern Oracle releases
Neither tool actually exists; both are hypothetical examples
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly distinguishes GoldenGate's own Data Pump process (shipping trail files) from the unrelated Oracle Data Pump export/import utility covered earlier in the course.

questions.q: Which scenario is a genuine real-world use case for GoldenGate rather than Data Guard?
options: A zero-downtime migration replicating ongoing changes from an old platform to a new one during cutover
Protecting a single Oracle database's availability with a synchronized standby
Automatically gathering optimizer statistics after a bulk load
Formatting an execution plan for a slow query
questions.explain: Zero-downtime migration, real-time integration, and active-active multi-region writes are GoldenGate's territory; protecting one Oracle database's availability is Data Guard's job.
